delta_findings.summary: parseActivationUrl reads ?source= from the URL string BEFORE any allowlist gate. An attacker who obtains ANY signed challengeless JWT — even one minted for a different user in a phishing scenario — can bypass the challenge check by appending source=whop-checkout to the URL. The security model REDUCES to 'the JWT signature is enough' for two source strings that are pure user-controlled input.
delta_findings.evidence: Line 203-209: sourceParam = url.searchParams.get('source'); source is trusted directly from the raw URL query. Line 216 + 371-372: TRUSTED_CHALLENGELESS_SOURCES.has(sourceParam) is the ONLY gate; no signature over the source claim, no cross-check that the JWT's `iss` matches whop-checkout backend.
delta_findings.reproduce: Construct liquidclips://activate?token=<any-valid-jwt>&source=whop-checkout — parser accepts, handler bypasses challenge, JWT stored.
delta_findings.suggested_fix: Bind the `source` to the JWT itself: include a signed `iss: 'whop-checkout'` claim in the backend-minted JWT. In activation.ts, only bypass challenge if the JWT's decoded `iss` matches the trusted source. The URL query is untrusted; only the signed JWT payload can be trusted. This is a defense-in-depth ask — the current model relies on 'attacker doesn't have any valid JWT' which is true today but reduces attack surface unnecessarily.

delta_findings.summary: Docstring at line 6-7 claims the hook 'emits flowTrace + PostHog telemetry' but the implementation only calls flowTrace() and postTick(). No PostHog capture. Documentation lie — the second half of the sentence is false.
delta_findings.evidence: Line 7: 'The local flowTrace + PostHog telemetry (existing)'. grep for 'posthog|capture|analytics.track' in the file returns zero matches beyond that comment.
delta_findings.suggested_fix: Either wire posthog.capture(actionId, {...}) alongside postTick, or delete the PostHog claim from the docstring. Silent docstring-vs-code drift is a Karpathy hidden-assumption pattern.

delta_findings.summary: Idempotency guard uses inflight.current ref; sets to true BEFORE setState({pending:true}) resolves. If the runner throws SYNCHRONOUSLY before the first await, the finally block resets inflight — that's fine — BUT the outer setState calls (lines 119, 151, 175) can also throw during unmount. If setState throws during a React unmount race, inflight stays true and the button is permanently disabled until app reload.
delta_findings.evidence: Line 178-179 finally { inflight.current = false } — inside try/catch wrapper of the runner only. setState calls at 119/151/175 are OUTSIDE the try. If component unmounts mid-fire and setState throws, finally still runs (it's in the outer scope's try/catch/finally) — actually verify: line 135 try wraps the runner, finally at 177 covers the try. React setState post-unmount just warns, doesn't throw. Low-probability edge case.
delta_findings.reproduce: Rapidly navigate away from TopHud during a fire() call.
delta_findings.suggested_fix: Move the setState({pending: true}) call INSIDE the try/finally so any exception in the state emit also resets inflight. Or accept the risk and downgrade to P2 — React's post-unmount setState is a console.warn not a throw in current React versions.

delta_findings.summary: _ACTION_COUNTS is defaultdict without a size cap. An attacker (or a bug that emits unique action_ids per click) can OOM the Railway instance by POSTing /audit/tick with a fresh action_id every request. No auth on the write path (per docstring line 10-11). No allowlist check on action_id at ingest.
delta_findings.evidence: Line 59-62: _ACTION_COUNTS = defaultdict(...) — grows unbounded. Line 89 (audit_tick) accepts any action_id string. Line 11: 'No auth (writes are cheap + telemetry-shaped)'.
delta_findings.reproduce: for i in {1..100000}; do curl -X POST https://api.jnremployee.com/audit/tick -H 'content-type: application/json' -d '{"action_id":"attack.'$i'","outcome":"failure"}' ; done
delta_findings.suggested_fix: Cap _ACTION_COUNTS at 200 entries (LRU eviction). OR gate ingest to only known action_ids matching a stable allowlist (/^[a-z][a-z0-9-]*\.[a-z0-9-]+$/ + max 100 unique per hour per IP). OR require the auth-optional shared-secret header used by other telemetry endpoints.

delta_findings.summary: useCallback dependency includes `runner` — every parent render that recreates the runner closure (which is almost every render, per the TopHud usage line 105 that inlines a new async function) invalidates the memo and fires a fresh `fire` reference. Downstream useEffects that depend on `signInAction.fire` would re-subscribe every render.
delta_findings.evidence: Line 180: `}, [actionId, backend, opts.surface, opts.userRef, runner])`. TopHud.tsx:105 passes `async () => { ... }` inline — new function every render.
delta_findings.suggested_fix: Use a ref to hold the latest runner + omit runner from the dep array. Standard pattern: `runnerRef.current = runner; useEffect(() => { runnerRef.current = runner })` OR document that consumers MUST useCallback their runner. TopHud consumer would need a fix too.

findings.summary: P0-001 fix is broken. In the shipped .app, LC_SHIPPED_RESOURCES_DIR is set to the Tauri resource_dir root (Contents/Resources) but tauri.conf.json entries `resources/node-*.gz` and `resources/remotion-bundle.tar.gz` bundle-preserve the `resources/` prefix — the actual files land at Contents/Resources/resources/*.gz. The Python resolver's fast path returns the env-var value verbatim, then does `resources / f"node-{os_kind}-{arch}.gz"` looking for Contents/Resources/node-darwin-arm64.gz which DOES NOT EXIST. Every shipped user hits missing-tarball, campaign-overlay renders fail with 'Remotion project not found'.
findings.evidence: Verified against the ACTUAL bundled .app at /Users/dipdip/code/jnr/desktop-2/src-tauri/target/release/bundle/macos/Liquid Clips.app/Contents/Resources/ — the pattern `Contents/Resources/_up_/_up_/python-sidecar/` and `Contents/Resources/_up_/dist/` proves Tauri v2 preserves the entry's path. Simulation output: env-var override resolves to `/simulated_app/Contents/Resources`, then `gz_path` = `/simulated_app/Contents/Resources/node-darwin-arm64.gz` exists=False; actual file at `/simulated_app/Contents/Resources/resources/node-darwin-arm64.gz`. See reproduce block.
findings.reproduce: python3 -c "import os; from pathlib import Path; os.makedirs('/tmp/sim/Contents/Resources/resources', exist_ok=True); os.makedirs('/tmp/sim/Contents/Resources/_up_/_up_/python-sidecar', exist_ok=True); Path('/tmp/sim/Contents/Resources/resources/node-darwin-arm64.gz').touch(); os.environ['LC_SHIPPED_RESOURCES_DIR']='/tmp/sim/Contents/Resources'; p = Path(os.environ['LC_SHIPPED_RESOURCES_DIR']).resolve(); gz = p / 'node-darwin-arm64.gz'; print('lookup:', gz, 'exists?', gz.exists()); print('actual:', p / 'resources' / 'node-darwin-arm64.gz', 'exists?', (p / 'resources' / 'node-darwin-arm64.gz').exists())"
findings.suggested_fix: Two clean options. (A) In Rust, pass the value with the `/resources` suffix appended so the env var matches Python's expectation: `app.path().resource_dir().ok().and_then(|p| p.canonicalize().ok()).map(|p| p.join("resources").to_string_lossy().to_string())`. (B) In Python, after resolving the override, first check if the tarballs are at the returned root; if not, try appending `/resources`. Option A is one line and localised; Option B is more defensive and also covers hand-set env vars. Do BOTH: A for correctness, B for defense-in-depth. Regression: extract the fresh bundled .app after the next build and verify `find Contents/Resources -name 'node-darwin-arm64.gz'` returns a path AND that the Python resolver's override branch finds it.

Next call returns cached=True + the corrupt path. Downstream ffmpeg composite fails with an opaque error.

findings.summary: Neither _atomic_extract_gz_to_file nor _atomic_extract_tar_to_dir fsyncs the PARENT DIRECTORY after os.replace. On sudden power loss (not SIGKILL), POSIX allows the directory rename entry to be lost even though the underlying inode/data was fsynced. Rare edge case; laptop crash during first-launch extraction could result in either final state or no state — not corruption, but the marker + rename discipline assumes ordering that fsync-on-parent guarantees.
findings.evidence: Standard POSIX documentation: an atomic rename is only durable across a crash if the containing directory is fsynced after the rename. Neither helper does `os.open(str(parent), os.O_RDONLY); os.fsync(fd); os.close(fd)` after os.replace.
findings.reproduce: No trivial local repro (requires actual power loss simulation). LWN reference: https://lwn.net/Articles/457667/
findings.suggested_fix: After each `os.replace(...)`, add a parent-dir fsync helper: `pfd = os.open(str(parent), os.O_RDONLY); try: os.fsync(pfd); finally: os.close(pfd)`. Skip on Windows where it's a no-op.

findings.evidence: sidecar.py:5186 `staging = parent / f'.{final_dir.name}.staging'` — same path every call. Line 5187 unconditionally rmtree's it. No fcntl.flock / lockfile / atomic-create-dir guard.

findings.suggested_fix: Either use tempfile.mkdtemp for a unique staging dir per invocation, or acquire an fcntl.flock on `<runtime_dir>/.extract.lock` around the extract+swap block. Prefer flock — keeps the disk-usage predictable.
